subject: Lyra Systems — Dedicated sizing, burst policy, and SL0 guardrails
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyra-systems.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Martins <sofia.martins@lyra-systems.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial capacity ask and burst expectations

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Lyra is excited about using Redwood Dedicated for inference on our realtime assistant and nightly batch embeddings. Before we move to a contract, my infra lead asked for a concrete sizing recommendation so we can provision our VPC and approve the capex window. High level:

- Peak realtime QPS: ~850 requests/minute during business hours (PST) with avg prompt length ~650 tokens.
- Nightly batch: 6M docs embeddings over a 6-hour window.
- Latency SLO for realtime: 95th <= 220ms token-latency at their p99 reply time constraint.

They want to understand how much dedicated capacity to reserve, how bursting works (for holiday spikes), and what guardrails we recommend to avoid overrun billing. Can you share a short playbook and a sample burst policy?

—Liam

---

Attachment: lyra_requirements_v1.pdf (summary)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyra-systems.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask and burst expectations

Liam —

Appreciate the detail. Quick reply with a plan outline; we'll follow up with numbers and an ops playbook. High-level approach:

1) Base reserved pool: size to meet steady-state realtime QPS + headroom for short bursts (we'll propose a baseline GPU count).
2) Burst layer: ephemeral GPU pool that can be used automatically for traffic surges. Billed at a higher rate but rate-capped via a monthly burst budget.
3) Batch window offload: use reserved nodes for low-priority batch jobs during nights; optional spot-backed workers for cost efficiency.
4) SLO enforcement: token-based throttles + graceful degradation rules (smaller model fallback, truncate-long prompts, or queue with 50ms accept window).

I'll loop in Marcus for the sizing spreadsheet and Priya for contractual burst budget language. Can you confirm your peak concurrency (850 req/min ~14.2 rps) is sustained for more than a 30-minute rolling window or is it a series of short spikes?

Thanks,
Sean

Signature:
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyra-systems.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 17:28:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Initial capacity ask and burst expectations — sizing draft attached

Hi Liam —

Attaching a quick model of recommended capacity and burst bands. Key assumptions are in tab A. TL;DR recommendations:

- Reserve: 8x A100-80GB equivalent (predicts steady-state realtime p95 latency ~180ms with 650-token avg using model: redwood-rt-3b-fp16).
- Burst pool: up to +4 GPUs for 8 hours/day during known business peaks; automatic attach when sustained 5-minute avg > 70% utilization on reserved pool.
- Burst budget: 250 GPU-hours/month included; above this billed at burst rate.
- Batch: schedule on reserved nodes in low traffic window, or offload to spot-backed ephemeral cluster to avoid interfering with realtime.

We also included suggested throttles: queue depth cap per org, prompt length cap, and automatic model-stepdown after 90s generation.

Attachment: lyra_multipass_headroom_model.xlsx

Let us know what to iterate on and any constraints (procurement/approval timelines).

—Marcus

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyra-systems.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial capacity ask and burst expectations — sizing draft attached

Hi Liam —

Good questions. Short answers:

- The "A100-80GB equivalent" is a performance-equivalent baseline reflecting our kernel+quantization stack; you do not need to procure exact vendor GPUs for our Dedicated offering — Redwood supplies the hardware. The number is to set expectations for throughput and to map to your internal procurement/finance templates.

- For peak weeks: we recommend a two-tier approach:
  * Emergency burst top-up: one-off negotiated top-up charge for predictable launch windows (we can sell a block of extra burst hours at a discounted uplift vs on-demand).
  * Autoscale soft cap: automatic failover to a compatible, lower-cost model variant when the burst budget is exhausted to maintain availability while controlling cost.

- We can also include a pre-approval workflow: you push a launch plan with expected burst multipliers and we pre-authorize additional headroom once it hits the approval threshold.

Neha is cc'd to outline the procurement language we'll add to the contract and the SLO/chargeback mechanics.

Best,
Priya

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyra-systems.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Contract language proposal: burst budget, pre-approval, and fallbacks

Liam —

Circling back with proposed clauses to add to the Dedicated Services Schedule. Highlights:

1) Burst Allowance: Customer is allocated 250 GPU-hours/month of burst capacity at the agreed burst rate. Unused burst hours do not roll over.

2) Emergency Top-up: Customer may request an Emergency Burst Top-up up to 1,000 GPU-hours for a single billed month, subject to prior written approval and a discounted block price (we propose 70% of on-demand).

3) Autoscale Soft Cap Behavior: Once allocated burst hours are consumed, Redwood will:
   - continue to accept requests but route excess traffic to a compatible lower-cost model variant, or
   - apply a customer-configurable queueing policy with a max wait time of 2 minutes, or
   - throttle incoming traffic to a fixed concurrency cap to preserve core SLOs.

4) Pre-Approval Workflow: Customer submits a Launch Plan via the Console/Drive link 72 hours before the expected spike; if approved, the top-up is auto-authorized.

5) Monitoring & Alerts: Redwood will emit token-level billing and GPU-hour burn metrics to the customer's Console and provide a daily projected-burn forecast during active bursts.

Attachment: proposed-burst-policy-2027.pdf

If that aligns, we'll attach an implementation schedule and get the DocuSign ready.

—Neha

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyra-systems.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sofia Martins <sofia.martins@lyra-systems.com>

Subject: Re: Contract language proposal: burst budget, pre-approval, and fallbacks

Neha/Team —

This all looks good and addresses Lyra's concerns. A couple of small asks before we sign:

- Can you add a clause to guarantee a 24-hour turnaround on Emergency Top-up approval during business days?
- Please confirm the data retention window for burst usage logs (Lyra will need 12 months for audit).

If those are fine, we can route the redlines to legal and get DocuSign moving. Thank you for being flexible on the launch-top-up pricing — that will make the procurement case much easier.

Regards,
Liam
